:::{.definition data-title="Sequence Convergence (Metric Spaces)"}

A [[sequence|sequence]] $\{x_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ in
[[knowledge-mathematics-analysis-functional-analysis-metric-spaces|metric space]]
$(X,d)$ is said to be convergent if there exists some **limit point** $x\in X$
such that
$$
\forall\epsilon>0,~\exists N\in\mathbb{N},~\forall n\geq N:d(x_n,x)<\epsilon~.
$$
We write $x_n\rightarrow x~(n\rightarrow \infty)$ or
$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}x_n=x$.

:::
